verdict: Chapters 3 and 4 contain no citations at all, so the gap statement in Section 3.1 rests on unsupported assertions; adding citations to the reviewed studies [1, 2, 10, 13, 19, 20, 21, 25, 28, 32] at the points indicated resolves this without any new references. The RQ-to-gap and RO-to-RQ traceability is sound in principle (each RO names its RQ), but the chapters are not submission-ready because of internal contradictions about research stage (the CA3 label, Tables 10 and 11 mapping RQ4–RQ6 to 'CA3' and to the wrong chapters, and the 'next stage will extend' sentence beside the implemented five-predicate rule), a dangling duplicate sentence in 4.7, and the redefinition of VL as the lifecycle predicate in Equation (30). The definitions of C, VI, VT, N = |G| and the five-predicate decision rule agree with Chapter 6, but component A must be reworded as 'authority requirements', VS must be reconciled with the composite VS(C, t, q) of Section 6.5, and VL needs an explicit definition linked to Equation (64).
